items.fromString:
The {{address-review-pr}} skill blocks on interactive prompts when running in CI pipelines, causing the session to end without completing its work.

## Problem

The skill asks for user input in several places:
- Dirty working tree: "ask user how to proceed"
- Comment categorization: "ask user to confirm"
- Ambiguous comments: "ask user for clarification"
- Pre-push hook failures: asks whether to use {{--no-verify}}

In CI there is no human to answer. The session hits max turns or times out while waiting.

## Evidence

In [build 2074442484376670208|https://prow.ci.openshift.org/view/gs/test-platform-results/logs/periodic-ci-openshift-hypershift-main-periodic-review-agent/2074442484376670208], the agent wrote correct test code, committed locally, but asked "Should I push with --no-verify?" and the session ended with no push.

## Fix

Add a {{--ci}} flag to the skill that makes all interactive prompts autonomous:
- Dirty tree: stash/discard
- Categorization: proceed without confirmation
- Ambiguous comments: decide autonomously or skip
- Pre-push hooks: {{--no-verify}} on pre-existing failures

Branch: https://github.com/enxebre/ai-helpers/compare/fix/address-review-ci-flag"}

<parameter name="additional_fields">{"parent": "CNTRLPLANE-3761"}

Claude requests permission to use {{mcp__plugin_golang_gopls__go_symbol_references}} during the solve phase but the permission is not granted, causing a tool error. The agent falls back to grep-based searching which works but is less precise and slower.

h2. Error

{noformat}Error: Claude requested permissions to use mcp__plugin_golang_gopls__go_symbol_references, but you haven't granted it yet.{noformat}

h2. Impact

* Claude loses access to LSP-powered symbol references (go-to-definition, find-references) and falls back to grep
* Grep-based fallback works but is noisier and slower for large codebases like hypershift
* May contribute to longer solve durations and higher token usage as Claude processes more irrelevant grep results

h2. Fix

Add gopls MCP tools to the {{--allowedTools}} list in the {{run_claude}} invocation for the solve phase in {{hypershift-jira-agent-process-commands.sh}}. Currently the solve phase allows:

{noformat}--allowedTools \"Bash Read Write Edit Grep Glob WebFetch Agent Skill Task\"{noformat}

Should also include {{mcp__plugin_golang_gopls__*}} or the specific tools like {{mcp__plugin_golang_gopls__go_symbol_references}}, {{mcp__plugin_golang_gopls__go_diagnostics}}.

Alternatively, use {{--permission-mode full}} or configure the gopls plugin permissions in the Claude Code settings.

items.fromString:
The jira-agent solve phase completes successfully — code changes are correct, tests pass, branch is pushed — but the process exits non-zero. This causes the harness to skip phases 2-4 (review, fix, PR creation), wasting the solve work.

h2. Evidence

In [build 2073051013308223488|https://prow.ci.openshift.org/view/gs/test-platform-results/logs/periodic-ci-openshift-hypershift-main-periodic-jira-agent/2073051013308223488] for CNTRLPLANE-3698:

* Claude's final message is a _success summary_ — it declares the task complete
* Session metrics show {{is_error: 0}} and {{stop_reason: end_turn}} — Claude finished normally
* The branch {{fix-CNTRLPLANE-3698}} was pushed with correct code changes
* {{make build}}, {{make test}}, {{make lint-fix}} all passed
* But {{agentic-ci run}} returned non-zero exit code

The same issue occurred in [build 2073016531159093248|https://prow.ci.openshift.org/view/gs/test-platform-results/logs/periodic-ci-openshift-hypershift-main-periodic-jira-agent/2073016531159093248] for CNTRLPLANE-3696.

h2. Where the exit code is captured

In {{hypershift-jira-agent-process-commands.sh}}, the {{run_claude()}} wrapper runs:

\{code}

agentic-ci run ... | grep '^\{'

local rc=$\{PIPESTATUS[0]\}

return $rc

\{code}

The exit code is {{agentic-ci}}'s, not Claude's conversation outcome. The harness then checks:

\{code}

if [ $EXIT_CODE -eq 0 ]; then

  # proceed to phases 2-4

else

  # mark as FAILED, skip everything

fi

\{code}

h2. Possible causes

h1. _agentic-ci propagates Claude Code's process exit code_ — Claude Code may exit non-zero when any {{Bash}} tool call during the session returned non-zero (e.g., {{gh pr create}} failing), even though Claude handled the error gracefully and completed the task

h1. _agentic-ci has its own error detection_ — it may inspect the OTEL stream or Claude's output for tool errors and decide to exit non-zero

h1. _Claude Code treats permission-denied tool calls as session failures_ — the MCP gopls tool permission error may contribute

h2. Investigation steps

h1. Run {{agentic-ci run}} locally with a prompt that includes a failing {{Bash}} command followed by a successful recovery, and check the exit code

h1. Check agentic-ci source for how it determines its exit code

h1. Check if Claude Code exits non-zero when tool errors occur mid-session but the session completes normally

h1. Compare with OCPBUGS-93785 and CNTRLPLANE-3697 runs where solve exited 0 — what was different?

h2. Mitigation (harness side)

Regardless of root cause, the harness should check for code changes (branch != main, diff exists) after the solve phase and proceed to phases 2-4 if changes are found, even when the exit code is non-zero. This is tracked separately in CNTRLPLANE-3760.

* [CNTRLPLANE-3698 transcript|https://gcsweb-ci.apps.ci.l2s4.p1.openshiftapps.com/gcs/test-platform-results/logs/periodic-ci-openshift-hypershift-main-periodic-jira-agent/2073051013308223488/artifacts/periodic-jira-agent/hypershift-jira-agent-process/artifacts/jira-agent-transcript.html]

h2. Problem

Our CI agentic workloads (jira-agent, review-agent) run Claude Code in Prow pods with GitHub tokens and Jira credentials exported as environment variables or configured via git credential helpers. The current security boundary relies on prompt-level instructions ("do not run {{git remote -v}}") which can be bypassed by prompt injection. We need a proper sandboxing model.

h2. Current state

* {{GITHUB_TOKEN}} is exported as an env var for {{gh}} CLI
* Git credential helper embeds the fork token in a shell function — {{git config credential.helper}} would print it
* Jira credentials are loaded from mounted secret files
* Security relies on {{--append-system-prompt}} instructions which are not a reliable boundary

h2. Desired state

h3. 1. Disallowed commands support in Claude Code CLI

Claude Code supports {{deny}} rules in {{.claude/settings.json}} for permission enforcement at the tool layer. We should be able to pass disallowed commands via CLI flags (e.g. {{--deny "Bash(git config credential.*)"}}) or write a {{settings.json}} before invocation. This would block sensitive commands regardless of prompt injection:

{code:json}{
  "permissions": {
    "deny": [
      "Bash(git config credential.*)",
      "Bash(git config --global credential.*)",
      "Bash(env)",
      "Bash(printenv)",
      "Bash(cat /var/run/claude-code-service-account/*)"
    ]
  }
}{code}

This is analogous to Carbonite's PreToolUse hook ({{egress-write-guard.py}}) which blocks write operations at the tool layer.

h3. 2. Container-level sandboxing (Carbonite model)

Carbonite provides a reference implementation for sandboxed Claude Code execution:

* *Network egress*: Squid proxy + nftables restrict outbound traffic to allowlisted hosts (AI APIs, VCS, Jira). This prevents credential exfiltration even if the model is compromised.
* *Filesystem*: Read-only mounts for credentials, writable scratch space for work.
* *Credentials*: Mounted as read-only files, never exported as env vars. The credential helper pattern leaks tokens via {{git config}} output.
* *Privilege ceiling*: {{no-new-privileges}} + user namespace isolation.
* {{--dangerously-skip-permissions}}: Safe when the container IS the security boundary.

For Prow, the equivalent would be:

* K8s NetworkPolicy restricting pod egress to AI inference + GitHub + Jira endpoints
* Secrets mounted read-only, not exported as env vars
* Potentially running Claude with {{--dangerously-skip-permissions}} if the pod isolation is sufficient

h3. 3. Credential isolation

Move from {{export GITHUB_TOKEN}} and inline credential helpers to:

* Read-only file mounts that Claude can't access directly
* A thin wrapper script that handles {{gh}} authentication without exposing the token to the Claude session
* Or a git credential helper that reads from a file Claude can't access (outside its working directory)

h3. *4. Skills have hooks short circuiting known undesired paths*

h3. 5. Skills/sandbox runner is intentional about [https://github.com/RedHatProductSecurity/prodsec-skills|https://github.com/RedHatProductSecurity/prodsec-skills|smart-link]  invocation

h2. Scope

* Evaluate whether {{.claude/settings.json}} deny rules are sufficient for CI
* Evaluate Carbonite's standalone (Podman) and OpenShell (K3s + Landlock) modes for CI adoption
* Implement the minimal viable sandboxing for the jira-agent and review-agent Prow jobs
* Document the security model for agentic CI workloads

* *Network egress*: Squid proxy + nftables restrict outbound traffic to allowlisted hosts (AI APIs, VCS, Jira). This prevents credential exfiltration even if the model is compromised.
* *Filesystem*: Read-only mounts for credentials, writable scratch space for work.
* *Credentials*: Mounted as read-only files, never exported as env vars. The credential helper pattern leaks tokens via {{git config}} output.
* *Privilege ceiling*: {{no-new-privileges}} + user namespace isolation.
* {{--dangerously-skip-permissions}}: Safe when the container IS the security boundary.

For Prow, the equivalent would be:

* K8s NetworkPolicy restricting pod egress to AI inference + GitHub + Jira endpoints
* Secrets mounted read-only, not exported as env vars
* Potentially running Claude with {{--dangerously-skip-permissions}} if the pod isolation is sufficient

h3. 3. Credential isolation

Move from {{export GITHUB_TOKEN}} and inline credential helpers to:

* Read-only file mounts that Claude can't access directly
* A thin wrapper script that handles {{gh}} authentication without exposing the token to the Claude session
* Or a git credential helper that reads from a file Claude can't access (outside its working directory)

h3. *4. Skills have hooks short circuiting known undesired paths*

h3. 5. Skills/sandbox runner is intentional about [https://github.com/RedHatProductSecurity/prodsec-skills|https://github.com/RedHatProductSecurity/prodsec-skills|smart-link]  invocation

h2. Scope

* Evaluate whether {{.claude/settings.json}} deny rules are sufficient for CI
* Evaluate Carbonite's standalone (Podman) and OpenShell (K3s + Landlock) modes for CI adoption
* Implement the minimal viable sandboxing for the jira-agent and review-agent Prow jobs
* Document the security model for agentic CI workloads
